title: finding(deps): @object-ui/layout and @object-ui/plugin-dashboard pin react in dependencies while also asking for it as a peer
body:
Found while implementing objectui#8198. That card removed the `react-dom` half of this defect from both packages because `react-dom` had no consumer, so the new gate could see it. The `react` half is invisible to that gate — `react` IS imported — and is left standing.

## Measured, on `e2409120f`

Two packages pin React at an exact version in `dependencies` while ALSO declaring a peer range for it:

| package | `dependencies.react` | `peerDependencies.react` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `packages/layout` | `19.2.8` | `^18.0.0 \|\| ^19.0.0` |
| `packages/plugin-dashboard` | `19.2.8` | `^18.0.0 \|\| ^19.0.0` |

No other released package does this. The house shape, in `plugin-charts`, `plugin-form`, `plugin-list` and the rest, is a peer range plus `@types/react` in `devDependencies` and nothing in `dependencies`.

## Why it matters

A library that both asks its host for React as a peer and installs an exact React of its own is making two contradictory statements. A consumer on React 18 satisfies the peer range and still gets a second, pinned React 19 pulled into their graph by these two packages. Two React copies in one tree is the classic cause of `Invalid hook call` — the failure is not at install time, it is at first render, and it does not point back here.

`peerDependencies` is one of the eight published-contract fields this repository's changeset gate watches, which is a reasonable proxy for how visible a change to this shape is; the fix is on the `dependencies` side and moves no peer.

## Likely fix, and the reason it is not a rider

Move the entry to `devDependencies` at the same pin, matching the packages that already do it — the local build and test run then still get a concrete React, and consumers get only the peer range. It is small, but it is a change to what two published packages install for every consumer, and objectui#8198's licence covered only declarations with NO consumer. It also interacts with objectui#8300 (the `react-dom` peer convention), so both should be looked at together.

Filed unassigned by the objectui#8198 implementation session.
